segments.headline: TOKENS
segments.narration: How does a decoder-only Transformer generate text? Start with: the cat sat. Tokenization turns text into discrete pieces. These word-sized tokens are only an illustration.

segments.headline: EMBEDDING + POSITION
segments.narration: Each token becomes an embedding vector. Position information lets the model distinguish order. Now the sequence is a set of numerical representations, ready to exchange information.

segments.headline: CAUSAL ATTENTION
segments.narration: In attention, each position produces a query, a key, and a value. Scaled query-key scores are masked: a position cannot access future tokens. Softmax converts allowed scores into weights.

segments.headline: MIX THE VALUES
segments.narration: For the last position, these illustrative weights mix the value vectors into a contextual representation. The arrows show information flow, not an explanation of the model’s reasoning.

segments.headline: MULTIPLE HEADS
segments.narration: Multiple attention heads perform different learned projections in parallel. Their outputs are concatenated and projected back into one representation. Different heads can capture different relationships.

segments.headline: STACK THE BLOCKS
segments.narration: Residual connections, normalization, and a token-wise feed-forward network complete a block. Stack many blocks to refine the representations. Exact normalization order varies across architectures.

segments.headline: NEXT-TOKEN DISTRIBUTION
segments.narration: At the final position, an output projection and softmax produce next-token probabilities. These example numbers are invented for illustration. A decoding rule selects the next token: on.

segments.headline: REPEAT
segments.narration: Append on to the context, then predict again. One token at a time, the sequence grows. That is autoregressive generation: the same Transformer, repeatedly applied.
